statement: Before promising that a recognition fix leaves every existing fixture unchanged, search the existing fixtures for the exact defect shape the fix removes. A card expected every existing behaviour-corpus specimen to score identically after extending v23's coverage-flag recognition to every rubric, and expected an existing test to pass unchanged; but one specimen's test script was 'vitest run --coverage', the very false absence the change withdraws, and the test pinned v22 still firing it. Both had to move. Rule: grep the fixtures for the defect's shape first, and report each one that must move as the fix's own measured delta, not as a regression to suppress.

When a stricter detector from one rubric is extended to rubrics that carry a looser one, add it to the looser rules rather than replacing them, or the 'fix' narrows recognition and creates new false absences. v23's reachability-checked coverage analysis drops credit v17 gives, such as an unreachable script named 'coverage'; replacing v17's heuristics with it would have asserted absences v17 never did. Rule: for a fix meant only to withdraw false absences, union the new recognition with the old, keep the old results first where order is read, and pin a control proving an old-only credit survives.
